subject: ventures/handyman-minimum-job-calculator
professional: a working handyman-business owner or a small-trades bookkeeper/estimator who sets minimum charges and trip fees; first check: is unpaid drive/estimate/supply time costed at the owner's pay target, is overhead spread over billable hours, does the break-even job size follow from the same inputs as the per-job floor

evidence.correctness: Ran sampleJob() through analyze() and recomputed independently in Python from the stated formulas. Trip hours (2x25+20+30)/60=1.6667; mileage 22x0.65=14.30; trip cost 1.6667x40+14.30=80.9667; minimum trip charge 80.9667/0.97=83.4708 (tool: 83.4708). Overhead 600/90=6.6667/hr; contribution 85x0.97-40-6.6667=35.7833; minimum job 80.9667/35.7833=2.2627 hrs, $192.33 (tool identical). Per-job: TV job cost (1.5+1.6667)x40+1.5x6.6667+25+14.30=175.967, floor 181.409, profit -30.467, effective hourly 30.379; bookcase cost 127.633, floor 131.581, eff 17.60; door cost 109.30, floor 112.680, eff 16.415; ladder 0.5h 10.888, 1h 23.056, 8h 61.238 - all match to 3 decimals. Algebra check: at h = minimum job hours, revenue after fee/overhead/mileage equals (h+trip)xowner pay, so the break-even and ladder are internally consistent (ladder flips to 'yes' between 2h and 3h, minimum job 2.26h). Caveat: independent only of the code, not of an external standard; no published handyman reference exists, so the check is my own re-derivation. Silent misparse of quoted thousands (see defects) is a wrong-number path, so not 4.
evidence.completeness: README/page claims checked: minimum trip charge (works), smallest job worth driving to at quoted rate (works, plus 'no job size covers the trip' warning when rate <= pay+overhead), lowest price per job (works), effective hourly with unpaid time (works), job-size ladder (works), CSV download (reportCsv tested, 10 columns), load-example, clear, local-only usage counters with opt-out (usage.mjs, 6 tests). 30/30 tests pass. All listed features work end to end; no stubs or TODOs found. Stage is still 'prototype' in VENTURE.yaml.
evidence.verification: Ran node --test calc.test.mjs page.test.mjs usage.test.mjs: 30 pass, 0 fail. Seeded three mutations in calc.mjs, reverted each with git checkout (git status clean after). (1) minimumTripCharge = tripCost*(1+fee) instead of /(1-fee): 24 pass, 0 fail - SURVIVED, the headline 'Minimum trip charge' number on the page is never asserted by any test (grep minimumTripCharge in *.test.mjs: no hits). (2) minimum-job hours divided by contribution+1: caught by 1 test. (3) mileage halved: caught by 2 tests. So the break-even and floor logic is guarded; the most prominent output is not. Tests are hand-calculated, which is good, but the parser has no test for quoted/thousands-separated numbers.
evidence.craft: Read calc.mjs (138 lines), calc.test.mjs, index.html script, usage.mjs. Clean pure functions, DOM-free, escaping via esc(), frozen defaults, input validation with named-field errors. Defects: CSV-style splitting on commas means '"1,200"' or '$1,200' in a number cell is split before cleaning, so materials/price are silently misread with no warning; num() maps non-numeric to NaN but parseJobs treats a bad materials/price cell as 0 for blank and only skips on NaN comparisons (NaN fails >=0 so it is skipped, ok) - the real hole is the comma case. Warning string is grammatically wrong for one job ('X pays' vs several: 'A, B, C pays'). canonical link is relative './index.html', which search engines ignore. Overheads on work hours only is a documented choice. Minor: HTML is a single 22KB file with inline CSS/JS, acceptable for this repo's pattern.
evidence.claims: Checked: 'nothing is uploaded' - page script imports only calc.mjs and usage.mjs, no fetch/XHR (page.test.mjs also asserts). Disclaimer present in header, FAQ and footer ('not legal, tax or licensing advice', no warranty, no SLA), README says 'Unverified against a real business's books', 'Sample data: an invented handyman business' shown. 'Works offline after the page loads' is plausible but not tested. 'Do Not Track switches counting off' - usage.mjs handles it. Problems: llms.txt links the tool to https://duncan-haywood.github.io/oss-monorepo/handyman-minimum-job-calculator/, the retired GitHub Pages address (production is marisstella.app, per VENTURE.yaml and README), so it points LLMs to a redirect/stale URL; sitemap/canonical not verified against production host. The FAQ claim 'A one-hour job at $85 an hour can keep less than half of that per hour' is backed by the sample ladder (1h -> $23.06, 27%), fine. No fake reviews or numeric market claims.
evidence.fitness: Walked the job: a handyman enters pay target 40, overhead 600/90 hrs, drive 25 min, 22 miles, 85/hr, pastes five jobs, clicks Calculate and gets a trip charge ($83.47), a minimum job (2.3 hrs / $192), a per-job floor and a verdict; the example result (every job under floor) is a striking and useful lesson. Gaps a real user would hit in the first hour: no handling of thousands separators in the job box (wrong numbers silently); no way to set a flat minimum visit fee and see what it does to the ladder; no tax/self-employment cost; materials get no markup so pass-through at cost with the card fee only; no saved state between visits, so a user re-types ten fields each time. Still usable for the stated job.
evidence.domain: Method: owner's pay target charged on every unpaid hour (drive both ways, estimate, supply run) plus per-mile vehicle cost, divided by (1 - payment fee) - this is the standard 'trip charge = cost of showing up' approach small-trades pricing coaches teach, and overhead = monthly overhead / billable hours is the usual shop-rate construction. Break-even job size as trip cost over per-hour contribution is correct. Departures a senior estimator would flag: no markup or profit margin above the owner's wage (the 'profit' is only profit over pay target), no tax or non-billable-admin load on overhead, overhead not charged on trip hours (defensible if billable-hours denominator excludes travel), fee applied to materials too (correct if materials are billed). The tool states these omissions openly.

defects.what: A comma inside a quoted or thousands-formatted number (e.g. "1,200" materials) is split into extra cells before cleaning, so materials and price are shifted and misread with no warning; the example I ran turned materials 1,200 / price 1,500 into materials 1 / price 200 and produced a plausible-looking result.
No test asserts minimumTripCharge, the headline output; a mutation changing /(1-fee) to *(1+fee) passed all 24 calc+page tests.
llms.txt points at the retired GitHub Pages host instead of https://marisstella.app/handyman-minimum-job-calculator/.
Canonical link is the relative './index.html', which search engines ignore.
Under-floor warning joins labels then says 'pays' (singular) for several jobs.
No markup/margin or tax load beyond the owner's wage; 'profit' is only profit over the pay target (stated in the column name, not hidden).

verdict: A small, honest, correct calculator: five independently recomputed outputs (trip charge, minimum job hours and price, per-job cost, floor, effective hourly, three ladder rows) match the code to three decimals, all 30 tests pass, every advertised feature works, and the disclaimer and unmodelled-items list are prominent. It falls short of the bar on verification (a seeded mutation to the headline minimum-trip-charge formula survived, because no test asserts that field), on claims (llms.txt links the retired host) and on craft (a thousands separator in the job box silently shifts columns and yields a wrong but plausible answer). None of this is hard to fix. Scored before any fix: meets the bar = no (verification 2, claims 2); finished = yes.
